stories.headline: Former PM Zapatero indicted in Plus Ultra airline rescue corruption case, triggering government crisis
stories.summary: Spain's Audiencia Nacional indicted former Socialist Prime Minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero on charges of influence-trafficking connected to the government's 2021 €53 million rescue of Venezuelan airline Plus Ultra. UDEF police reports attribute Zapatero 'strategic supervision' of an influence network with connections to Venezuela, China, and offshore structures; the indictment, arrived shortly after PSOE's worst-ever Andalusia election result, triggered intense political debate about early elections, coalition stability, and PSOE's future.

stories.headline: PP wins Andalusia election but loses majority, needs Vox to form government
stories.summary: The People's Party won Sunday's Andalucía regional election under incumbent president Juanma Moreno but lost its absolute majority, leaving it dependent on far-right Vox to form a government. The PSOE suffered its worst-ever result in the region at 22.7%, while Vox gained seats; post-election negotiations between PP and Vox began, with Vox demanding conditions comparable to agreements in Extremadura and Aragón.

stories.headline: Feijóo puts PP on full electoral alert, vows party is ready for snap election
stories.summary: PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo ordered the party to enter permanent 'electoral mode' following the Andalusia victory and the Zapatero scandal, instructing regional barons and mayors to mobilize voter networks. Feijóo repeatedly attacked the government over corruption while resisting Vox pressure to file an immediate no-confidence motion, arguing the arithmetic does not guarantee success.

stories.headline: Mass anti-government protest in Madrid draws tens of thousands demanding Sánchez resignation
stories.summary: Sociedad Civil Española convened a large march in central Madrid on Saturday, May 23, attended by tens of thousands demanding Sánchez's immediate resignation amid the Zapatero corruption case; PP and Vox leaders joined the march. The event ended with three arrests and seven police officers injured, and a separate incident involving attacks on journalists from TVE and La Sexta was reported.

stories.headline: Abascal meets new US Ambassador, shares concerns about Spain's corruption crisis
stories.summary: Vox leader Santiago Abascal held a meeting lasting over an hour with the newly arrived US Ambassador to Spain, Benjamín León Jr., on Friday May 22, discussing the 'grave situation' he attributes to the Sánchez government's corruption scandals; the meeting drew comment after it emerged the ambassador had also held meetings with PP's Feijóo and Madrid president Ayuso in the same period. Commentary in the Spanish press noted the US intelligence services' role in the Zapatero investigation.

stories.headline: Vox internal crisis: purge of Antelo leaves PP without Cartagena mayoralty
stories.summary: Santiago Abascal's purge of Vox's Murcia regional president José Ángel Antelo in February triggered ongoing internal instability; two expelled officials publicly criticized Abascal's 'personalismo,' and the departure of Vox municipal councillors in Cartagena cost PP the mayoralty. Abascal is nonetheless expected to lead Vox again in the 2027 general election.

stories.headline: Yolanda Díaz faces criminal complaint from Julio Iglesias over abuse comments
stories.summary: Singer Julio Iglesias proceeded to file a criminal complaint for libel and slander at the Supreme Court against Deputy PM and Labor Minister Yolanda Díaz, who had publicly endorsed allegations that Iglesias subjected domestic staff to 'slavery-like' conditions. Díaz refused to retract her statements, with her ministry citing freedom of expression; the case follows a failed conciliation hearing.

stories.headline: Sumar fractures left-wing space as ERC's Rufián offers to lead new progressive front
stories.summary: ERC's congressional spokesperson Gabriel Rufián publicly offered to lead a new left-wing electoral front for the 2027 general election, rattling the parties that make up Sumar's coalition (IU, Comuns, Más Madrid, Movimiento Sumar). Yolanda Díaz, who has confirmed she will not stand again, effectively endorsed Rufián; Podemos backed a different arrangement with Irene Montero, while Adelante Andalucía rejected any pact.

stories.headline: Yolanda Díaz challenges PP to file no-confidence motion; PP declines
stories.summary: Labor Minister and Deputy PM Yolanda Díaz publicly challenged PP leader Feijóo to file a no-confidence motion if the party believed the government was corrupt, citing the Zapatero case; Díaz also called on Zapatero to give explanations 'quickly.' PP's Senate spokeswoman Alicia García rejected the challenge as 'outrageous,' and PP Secretary-General Tellado reiterated that filing a motion that would fail would 'hand Sánchez a victory.'

stories.headline: Yolanda Díaz China visit: promotes SAIC electric vehicle investment, draws criticism
stories.summary: Deputy PM Yolanda Díaz visited China to promote investment, praising Chinese automaker SAIC as a 'giant of green mobility' and discussing a potential SAIC electric vehicle factory in Galicia. Her trip drew criticism from political opponents for not challenging the Chinese government on human rights; she was also photographed with a crutch on alternating arms, sparking social media commentary.

stories.headline: Spain government announces job-matching programme for half a million undocumented migrants
stories.summary: Spain's government unveiled a plan to match migrants to jobs under a regularisation programme aimed at granting legal status to approximately 500,000 undocumented workers; the plan was described by Spain's top immigration official in an interview with Reuters. The programme, announced in January, has drawn criticism from far-right parties domestically and across Europe.

stories.headline: Thousands protest housing costs in Madrid; government faces political pressure on crisis
stories.summary: Thousands rallied in central Madrid on Sunday against spiraling housing costs that have priced many Spaniards out of the market, particularly in Madrid and Barcelona. The housing crisis is described as one of Prime Minister Sánchez's key political vulnerabilities ahead of 2027 elections; the government passed a €7 billion housing plan last month.

stories.headline: Spain protests Bilbao police handling of Gaza flotilla activists; Israel demands explanation
stories.summary: Around two thousand protesters gathered in Bilbao to condemn Basque police treatment of Gaza flotilla activists on their return from Israeli detention; Spain was among Western governments that expressed anger after Israeli minister Ben-Gvir mocked the activists on video. The Israeli Embassy demanded an 'explanation' from the Spanish government.

stories.headline: Felipe VI official visit to Canada: school reunion, Margaret Atwood prize, cultural diplomacy
stories.summary: King Felipe VI completed an official visit to Canada during the week, highlighted by an emotional return to Lakefield College School in Ontario where he studied in 1984–85; he also delivered the Joan Margarit International Poetry Prize to Margaret Atwood in Toronto. The visit generated extensive royal coverage in Spain.
